title: Splitting an 'average of a subset' problem
idea: MEET: decompose a problem whose sub-problems FEED each other — filter, then total-and-count the filtered items, then divide — an ordered chain.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: 'Find the average of just the passing scores (pass is 60+).' The OUTPUT is...
options: the average of the passing scores
exercises.explanation: One output: the average of the subset that passed. But getting there needs several ordered steps.

exercises.prompt: By hand: scores are 50, 70, 90, 40, 80. Which PASS (60+)?
exercises.explanation: 70, 90, 80 are 60 or more. The passing subset has 3 scores.

exercises.prompt: Same example — the average of the passing scores is...
exercises.explanation: Total the passers: 240. Count them: 3. 240 / 3 = 80. That's our check value.

exercises.prompt: Order the sub-problems for this chained problem.
blocks: Filter: keep only the passing scores
Total the passing scores and count them
Divide the passing total by the passing count
exercises.explanation: Filter first (you need the subset), then total/count that subset, then divide. Each step feeds the next.

exercises.prompt: Why must 'filter the passing scores' come FIRST?
options: The later steps work ONLY on the passing subset
Filtering is always first in every problem
exercises.explanation: Total, count, and divide all operate on the passers — so you must isolate them before anything else.

exercises.prompt: Select the dependencies in this plan.
options: divide depends on the total and count
divide depends on the filter directly only
exercises.explanation: Filter feeds total/count; total/count feed divide. The filter does NOT depend on the divide.

exercises.prompt: This problem has one output but still needs several ordered sub-problems.
exercises.explanation: Yes — one output doesn't mean one step. Reaching the average of a subset is a chain of three jobs.

exercises.prompt: EDGE CASE: what if NO scores pass? What goes wrong in the last step?
options: Dividing by a count of 0 — we must guard against it
Nothing — 0 is fine to divide by
exercises.explanation: An empty subset means dividing by zero. The average-with-empty-guard (Unit 79) handles this. Edge cases matter.

exercises.prompt: Match each sub-problem to its pattern.
exercises.explanation: Filter, accumulate, divide — three familiar patterns chained in order make the subset average.

options: Chained sub-problems (filter -> total/count -> divide) run in a forced order, with an empty guard
exercises.explanation: When sub-problems feed each other, the order is forced — and don't forget the edge case guard.
